extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting articles to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, uploading, and verifying a scholarly article submission to arXiv, including allowed formats, metadata, moderation, and post‑submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topicality and refereability
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv should be topical and refereeable scientific contributions that follow accepted standards of scholarly communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic acceptance criterion for content: non-scientific material or content that is not topical/refereeable may be rejected. Submissions are subject to moderation to verify appropriateness and topicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered author requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We only accept submissions from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New users or those submitting to a new category may be required to obtain endorsements. See endorsement instructions if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and content removal
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are subject to a moderation process that verifies material is appropriate and topical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material that contains offensive language, non-scientific content, or is plagiarized may be removed. Authors must follow the moderation policy; moderation decisions determine acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrevocable license to distribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must grant arXiv.org an irrevocable license to distribute the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting distribution rights is a mandatory part of submission; authors must agree to licensing terms before public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to submission and site policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must agree to the Submittal Agreement, code of conduct, moderation, and privacy policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement to these policies is required to complete submission; read and accept the listed policies as part of the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-submission expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to self-submit; third-party submissions are accepted only under limited conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a proxy/third-party submission route, follow the specific instructions for third-party and index submissions for conference proceedings. Default expectation is that the registering author performs the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and announcement schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: New submissions received by 14:00 (Eastern) are generally made available at 20:00 (Eastern) according to the schedule for availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits and final submission before 14:00 EDT/EST Monday–Friday will not delay announcement. Unsubmitting or resubmitting can change announcement scheduling; check the schedule of availability and versions help pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and accepted text formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted submission formats (in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX, (La)TeX Markup, PDF, HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is long-term portable formats; (La)TeX is preferred. The page also states arXiv does not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source, and does not accept scanned documents, regardless of format. Use PDFLaTeX if using PDF/JPEG/PNG figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure formats: PostScript (PS, EPS) — requires LaTeX processing; JPEG, GIF, PNG or PDF figures — requires PDFLaTeX processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixed figure formats according to the chosen compiler will cause compilation failures. Ensure figure formats match the engine (PDFLaTeX vs (La)TeX) and convert figures ahead of upload if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No externally linked/omitted figures allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide links to view figures externally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figure files referenced in the submission must be uploaded as part of the submission package; external hosting of figures is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard macro packages for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., graphics and graphicx) to have figures appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues; following standard macros reduces processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File names containing other characters (spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will be rejected. This restriction ensures portability and archival safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv's system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly. Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are different; mismatches are a common source of failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of ancillary files (data, code, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files associated with articles; follow separate instructions for including data sets and ancillary files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate ancillary files instructions; do not assume full general-purpose data hosting. Use supported packaging (zip or tar.gz) to include ancillary files when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare title and abstract for inclusion in metadata following separate instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and abstract metadata are used on abstract pages, in announcements, and in RSS feeds; follow the separate guidance to improve discoverability and ensure correct metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-level TeX detection and file selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission system auto-detects the correct processor and the top-level TeX file(s). Only TeX files containing \documentclass directives are shown as top-level candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the auto-detected notes, compiler choice, and the file detected as Top-Level TeX. You may choose a different compiler or different top-level files; you may choose multiple top-level files and arXiv will concatenate their outputs in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: File check/compilation and review step
rubrics_metrics.description: After upload, click 'Check Files' to have files analyzed; the system will display compilation log and whether compilation succeeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compiled successfully, preview the PDF and continue to Metadata. If compilation fails, review common mistakes listed and correct before final submission. Note which files are recommended for deletion and uncheck if they should be kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common compilation problems to check
rubrics_metrics.description: Five most common mistakes: mixed figure file formats relative to compiler; file-name upper/lower-case mismatch between TeX source and included files; default hyperref failures are not a reason to report a failure (continue to find specific errors); missing customized or differing versions of style files; missing, misnamed, or local complete paths to figure files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these common issues before contacting arXiv support. arXiv does not perform figure file conversion; ensure formats and paths are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and correct before final submit; unsubmit procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final 'Submit Article' step, carefully check title, abstract (metadata), and processed files. If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, use 'Unsubmit' to return it to incomplete status and modify files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting takes the article out of the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time. Edits and final submission before 14:00 Eastern generally will not delay announcement. Do not create a new submission for a corrected article or erratum — replace the original submission instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and date stamp rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No additional versions are generated when edits are done before the submission is publicly announced; the date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware the public date is set at final submission; replacing the original submission (not creating a new one) is the correct way to correct content prior to announcement. See versions help pages for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission availability and related pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about availability of submissions and public availability schedule is provided in dedicated 'Availability of submissions' and 'public submission availability' pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the public submission availability page for details on when submissions become available, and check related help pages (versions, schedule of availability) for timing and access policies.
